description_json.name: AtbashWithCasePreservation
description_json.idea: A classic Atbash cipher that reverses the alphabet (A to Z, B to Y, etc.) while preserving the exact case of each letter. Numbers, spaces, and punctuation marks remain completely unchanged. This is a highly intuitive, symmetric, and reversible single-character substitution cipher that is extremely easy for LLMs to reason about while completely altering the token representation of words.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
For each character in the input text:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), replace it with the letter at the symmetric position in the uppercase alphabet: ciphertext_char = chr(155 - ord(plaintext_char)). For example, 'A' (65) becomes 'Z' (90), and 'B' (66) becomes 'Y' (89).
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), replace it with the letter at the symmetric position in the lowercase alphabet: ciphertext_char = chr(219 - ord(plaintext_char)). For example, 'a' (97) becomes 'z' (122), and 'b' (98) becomes 'y' (121).
3. If it is a digit, space, punctuation mark, or any other symbol, leave it exactly as it is.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
Since the Atbash cipher is its own inverse (symmetric), the decryption rules are identical to the encryption rules:
1. If it is an uppercase letter (A-Z), replace it with: plaintext_char = chr(155 - ord(ciphertext_char)).
2. If it is a lowercase letter (a-z), replace it with: plaintext_char = chr(219 - ord(ciphertext_char)).
3. If it is any other character, leave it unchanged.

description_json.idea: A fixed one-to-one substitution over the English alphabet. Each plaintext letter is replaced by exactly one ciphertext letter using a single bijection, and the mapping is the same for uppercase and lowercase letters. Non-letter characters are left unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules: Use the following bijection: plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz -> ciphertext alphabet qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm. Thus a->q, b->w, c->e, d->r, e->t, f->y, g->u, h->i, i->o, j->p, k->a, l->s, m->d, n->f, o->g, p->h, q->j, r->k, s->l, t->z, u->x, v->c, w->v, x->b, y->n, z->m. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules: Use the inverse bijection: ciphertext alphabet qwertyuiopasdfghjklzxcvbnm -> plaintext alphabet abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz. Thus q->a, w->b, e->c, r->d, t->e, y->f, u->g, i->h, o->i, p->j, a->k, s->l, d->m, f->n, g->o, h->p, j->q, k->r, l->s, z->t, x->u, c->v, v->w, b->x, n->y, m->z. Uppercase letters use the same mapping, preserving case. All non-letter characters remain unchanged.

ciphers.name: Base36AlternateBlockTransposition

description_json.name: Base36 Alternate Block Transposition
description_json.idea: Divide the text into blocks of 2 characters. For each block, swap the two characters. If the text has an odd length, the last character remains in place. This is a simple, reversible transposition cipher that does not alter the characters themselves, making it extremely easy for LLMs to process and reason about while disrupting tokenization and simple pattern matching.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
1. Split the input string into pairs of characters (blocks of size 2).
2. For each pair, swap the first and second character (e.g., 'ab' becomes 'ba').
3. If the string has an odd number of characters, the final single character at the end remains unchanged.
4. All characters, including spaces, punctuation, digits, and casing, are treated exactly the same and swapped according to their positions.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
1. Split the ciphertext string into pairs of characters (blocks of size 2).
2. For each pair, swap the first and second character (e.g., 'ba' becomes 'ab').
3. If the string has an odd number of characters, the final single character at the end remains unchanged.

description_json.name: VowelConsonantShift
description_json.idea: A simple, highly readable substitution cipher designed to minimize LLM reasoning errors. It shifts vowels to the next vowel in the sequence (a->e, e->i, i->o, o->u, u->a) and consonants to the next consonant in the alphabet, preserving case. Numbers, spaces, and punctuation remain completely unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
1. Identify if the character is a letter. If not, keep it unchanged.
2. If it is a vowel (a, e, i, o, u), shift it to the next vowel in the circular sequence: a -> e, e -> i, i -> o, o -> u, u -> a. Maintain uppercase/lowercase (e.g., A -> E, U -> A).
3. If it is a consonant, shift it to the next consonant in the alphabetical sequence, skipping vowels: b->c, c->d, d->f, f->g, g->h, h->j, j->k, k->l, l->m, m->n, n->p, p->q, q->r, r->s, s->t, t->v, v->w, w->x, x->y, y->z, z->b. Maintain uppercase/lowercase (e.g., B -> C, Z -> B).
description_json.decrypt_rules:
1. Identify if the character is a letter. If not, keep it unchanged.
2. If it is a vowel, shift it to the previous vowel in the circular sequence: e -> a, i -> e, o -> i, u -> o, a -> u. Maintain uppercase/lowercase.
3. If it is a consonant, shift it to the previous consonant in the alphabetical sequence, skipping vowels: c->b, d->c, f->d, g->f, h->g, j->h, k->j, l->k, m->l, n->m, p->n, q->p, r->q, s->r, t->s, v->t, w->v, x->w, y->x, z->y, b->z. Maintain uppercase/lowercase.
